title: Route matrix spec and validation checklist
body:
Purpose:
This note defines a pragmatic, testable 'route matrix' configuration model for the control plane, plus validation rules and an operational canary/rollout checklist. The aim is to support multi-dimensional routing (region, customer tier, latency targets, model variant), enable lightweight validation pre-publish, and make progressive rollouts simple and auditable.

Context and design goals:
- Support expressive rules without exploding combinatorics: matchers, weight matrices, fallbacks.
- Deterministic evaluation order and clear precedence semantics.
- Validation that catches common OOB errors (weight sums, invalid regions, incompatible model variants) before service disruption.
- Rollout primitives: versioned configs, canary percentages, time windows, metric gates, automatic rollback triggers.
- Multi-region and geo-affinity controls: prefer local replicas, configurable cross-region fallback.

High-level model: route-matrix is an ordered list of route-entries. Each entry has: matcher, matrix (weights by backend), constraints, metadata, rollout policy (optional). During evaluation the control plane finds the first matcher that matches the request and selects a backend based on the matrix and runtime constraints.

Key terms (brief):
- matcher: boolean predicate over request attributes (region, customer_id, model, headers, tokens, latency_sla).
- backend: a logical serving target (hosted model version, dedicated pool, private endpoint).
- weight matrix: distribution among candidate backends; supports direct weights and conditional weights (e.g., weights that depend on request size).
- rollout policy: describes staged rollout parameters tied to a config version (canary_pct, duration, metric_gates).

Recommended fields for route-entry (explanatory, not strict JSON schema):
- id: short id string
- description: human note
- matcher: expression language string (see examples)
- backends: list of backend refs (name, region, capacity_tier, tags)
- weights: list aligned to backends (integers or percentages; may include conditional expressions)
- fallback: backend ref or null
- constraints: {max_latency_ms, min_qps, require_encryption, allowed_regions} (note: stored as flat fields in implementation)
- rollout: {version, canary_pct, step_intervals, metric_gates, auto_rollback}
- meta: owner, ticket, created_at

Example matcher language (simple rules):
- region == "eu-west-1" && customer_tier in ("enterprise","partner")
- header.x-experiment == "variantA"
- tokens <= 1024 && model == "redwood-advanced-v2"

Example compact YAML config (human readable):

---
- id: "enterprise-eu-routing"
  description: "Prefer enterprise dedicated pool in EU, fallback to hosted eu-optim"
  matcher: "region == 'eu-west-1' && customer_tier == 'enterprise'"
  backends:
    - name: "dedicated-eu-enterprise-v1"
      region: "eu-west-1"
      tags: ["dedicated","enterprise"]
    - name: "hosted-eu-optim-v2"
      region: "eu-west-1"
      tags: ["hosted","low-latency"]
  weights: [90, 10]
  fallback: "hosted-global-fallback-v1"
  constraints:
    max_latency_ms: 200
    min_qps: 10
    allowed_regions: ["eu-west-1","eu-central-1"]
  rollout:
    version: "v2024-09-12-1"
    canary_pct: 5
    step_intervals: [10m, 30m, 1h]
    metric_gates:
      p50_latency_ms: {threshold: 250, comparison: "<=", breach_action: "rollback"}
      error_rate_pct: {threshold: 0.5, comparison: "<=", breach_action: "rollback"}
    auto_rollback: true

Validation and pre-publish checks (automated):
1) Syntax: YAML/JSON parse.
2) Reference integrity: all backend names must exist in backend registry and be compatible with requested model versions.
3) Weight sanity: weights present and sum > 0. Prefer normalizing to percentages. Warn if sum != 100 but allow weighted ratios.
4) Region/replica check: for region-affinity matchers, ensure at least one backend in the matched region or a permitted cross-region fallback exists.
5) Constraint feasibility: verify constraints are feasible against capacity metadata (e.g., min_qps <= provisioned_qps).
6) Rollout sanity: canary_pct between 0 and 50 (default max 10 for initial canaries), step_intervals are monotonic positive durations, metric_gates reference valid telemetry metrics.
7) Security flags: if require_encryption true, target backends must support TLS+KMS key id.
8) Forbidden patterns: disallow using both "private" and "hosted" tags in a single backend list when config path is under a private tenant scope.

JSON Schema (illustrative) - for automated validators (flattened values are OK):
{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#","type":"object","required":["id","matcher","backends","weights","rollout"],"properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"matcher":{"type":"string"},"backends":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","required":["name","region"],"properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"region":{"type":"string"},"tags":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}}}},"weights":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"}},"fallback":{"type":["string","null"]},"constraints":{"type":"object"},"rollout":{"type":"object","properties":{"version":{"type":"string"},"canary_pct":{"type":"number"},"step_intervals":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"metric_gates":{"type":"object"},"auto_rollback":{"type":"boolean"}}}}

Rollout mechanics (operational runbook):
- Publish flow:
  1) Author config in staging branch (file under /configs/staging).
  2) Run "routing-validate" CI job which runs the schema checks + registry lookups + integration smoke tests (see below).
  3) Create an immutable config version token and upload to control plane staging bucket.
  4) Canary release: set canary_pct and start at time T0. Canary period default 30m for small changes, 2h for model variant swaps.
  5) During canary: monitor metric_gates (p50/p95 latency, error_rate, tail-qos, unit_cost_token). Gate evaluation cadence: 1m for latency, 5m for error_rate/cost.
  6) If gates pass for consecutive windows (configurable: default 3 windows), advance to next step (e.g., 25%, then 50%). If any gate breaches, trigger auto_rollback if enabled, else pause and notify on-call.
  7) After reaching 100%, mark config version as active and record promotion in audit log (who, when, ticket).

Canary sizing guidance:
- Start at small absolute RPS: for low-traffic customers use min( max(available_qps * 0.02, 1), 10 ) as initial canary qps cap.
- For global configs, prefer percentage-based canaries with a hard cap to avoid overloading new backends.

Metric gates (suggested default set):
- p50_latency_ms: <= baseline + 30%
- p95_latency_ms: <= baseline + 50%
- error_rate_pct: <= baseline + 0.2
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: <= baseline + 20%
- model_quality_regressions: zero regressions on golden prompt set (external eval hook)

Multi-region specifics and consistency model:
- Region affinity: specify allowed_regions in constraints. When allowed_regions includes multiple regions, the control plane will prefer same-region backends at selection time when available.
- Cross-region fallback: controlled by fallback policy with explicit allowed cross-region list. Cross-region calls should add a tracing header to account for egress billing and increased latency.
- Replica tags: backends have tags like region:eu-west-1, replica-class:hot/warm. Use constraints to prefer hot replicas for latency sensitive workloads.
- Stale config propagation: control plane publishes delta updates; edge proxies accept new config versions and expose a 'config_applied' timestamp. Rollouts must wait for N-of-M proxies in region to ack before moving to next phase (default N=M*0.8).

Control plane interactions and atomicity:
- Configs are versioned and immutable once published. A publish transaction creates a new version and sets target scope (global, tenant, region).
- Activation uses a two-phase commit: publish -> nominate (canary) -> activate. Nomination pins a small percentage traffic to the new version while the rest remains on previous.
- The control plane must expose APIs: validate(config), publish(config) -> version, set_rollout(version, policy), status(version) -> {phase, health}, rollback(version) -> previous_version.

Testing & smoke test checklist (CI + staging):
- unit tests for matcher language parsing and evaluation with edge-case inputs.
- integration tests that spin up a fake backend registry and assert selection logic (weighting + fallbacks).
- load-limited smoke: route synthetic traffic through staging proxies and assert metric gates (latency within 2x baseline) before canary.
- golden prompt regression check: for model variant swaps, run a discrete eval harness against saved prompt set.

Operational checklist before publishing a high-risk route change:
- [ ] Author and peer review of config (link to PR).
- [ ] routing-validate CI green.
- [ ] Staging smoke pass (end-to-end).
- [ ] On-call and SRE informed with runbook link.
- [ ] Canary policy set with metric gates and alert hooks.
- [ ] Audit ticket linked (ticket id in meta).

Common failure modes and recommended mitigations:
- Weight misconfiguration (e.g., all zeros): pre-publish abort; in-flight safety net: default traffic steering to last-known-good version.
- Region mismatch: validation fails; if missed, auto-detect high latency and rollback or divert to global fallback.
- Backend degradation during canary: trigger rollback, scale warm replicas if capacity permits.
- Telemetry gaps: prevent rollout progression until metrics pipeline shows healthy ingestion for 5m.

Appendix A: matcher examples and evaluation order:
1) explicit customer matcher (high priority)
2) region + tier matcher
3) model-specific matcher
4) catch-all default route

Appendix B: sample policy for emergency traffic-shift (fast-fail):
- Emergency endpoint accepts config "emergency-shift" which maps traffic to a specified safe backend immediately (bypasses canary). Requires 2-person auth.

Notes / open questions:
- Should weight matrices accept dynamic expressions referencing current cluster load? (pro: adaptive; con: harder to validate and reason about).
- How to best represent multi-tenant private endpoints in the same schema while ensuring no accidental cross-tenant leakage? Ideas: explicit scope field + validator that enforces backend scope.
- Integrate model quality evaluation (golden set) as a first-class metric in metric_gates (requires faster eval infra).
